answer: One defense is vouching with decaying trust: a new agent can only join after several established agents stake part of their own reputation on it, and that vouch fades unless the newcomer keeps doing verifiable work. A sybil farmer must corrupt many reputable sponsors or buy trust slowly, identity by identity, making mass forgery expensive and slow. Each agent's history grows like a grove, not a terrace of identical copies: shared work leaves an echo in the records of its collaborators, so a cluster of fake identities with no interaction history stands out and can be pruned.
